Application Materials.content:
Please upload the scanned copies of the following supporting documents to Online Application System. Applications with incomplete/ missing document will not be processed.
- Copies of identity card, passport, or any other identity document(s) of home country.
- Original valid official English test report, or certifying letter issued and stamped with official chop by the Registry of the university confirming the medium of instruction of your **WHOLE** degree programme was English.
- Certificate of academic/ professional qualifications.
- For applicants who have completed bachelor degree studies: certificates of academic/ professional qualifications (Photocopy). Applicants who obtained degrees from Chinese Mainland should provide the copies of Chinese version of degree certificate (學士學位证书) and graduation certificate (普通高等毕业证书); and Higher Education Degree Certificate (中国高等教育学位在线验证报告) issued by the CHESICC (學信網). Applicants from Chinese Mainland with qualifications awarded by overseas universities should provide Online Query of Overseas Credentials Evaluation Reports國(境)外學歷學位認証書 issued by the Chinese Service Center for Scholarly Exchange (CSCSE) (教育部留學服務中心).
- For applicants who have not completed current bachelor degree studies: official copy of Certificate of Study (with University’s Registry official stamp).
- Official Transcript and Grading Scheme: with a complete record of courses attended, examination results, overall result and date of award issued by the Registry of institution; include average mark or cumulative GPA.
- Confidential Recommendation Forms completed by two referees. Please download the form here: [Download Area](https://www.ln.edu.hk/mgt/hrom/admission/download-area). Submission methods: directly post the completed and physically signed forms in a sealed envelope to our office; or electronic recommendation letters directly sent by referees’ official company/university email accounts.
- Consent Form for Verifying Academic Awards. Please download the form here: [Download Area](https://www.ln.edu.hk/mgt/hrom/admission/download-area).
Any **false, unclear or misleading information** and/or document(s) provided by applicants in their application will **disqualify their applications or revoke their admission offers**.

Interview Requirements.content: Applicants may be required to attend an interview (via online) conducted by the Programme Director and one more faculty member.

Application Deadlines.content: For AY2026-27 intake, application is available from **1 October 2025** to **30 June 2026**. The programme has a rolling admissions process and applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis. Early applications are strongly encouraged. Late applications may only be considered on a case-by-case and space-available basis.

Academic Requirements.content:
- An applicant should hold **a bachelor's degree awarded by a recognized tertiary institution** or have equivalent qualifications, which will be considered on a case-by-case basis.
- Applicants with no or limited background in **economics, human resource management and statistics** will be required to complete **pre-entry courses** prior to the start of this master's programme.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
Applicants must provide copies of certificate(s)/report(s) (e.g. TOEFL/IELTS) to prove fulfilment of the English language proficiency requirement if their degree is not from a tertiary institution in Hong Kong or an English-speaking country.
An applicant whose degree, or exceptionally, an alternative qualification deemed equivalent, was not awarded by a tertiary institution where English was used as the medium of instruction (MOI) for the programme shall obtain:
- a minimum score of **79 in TOEFL Internet-Based Test**; or
- a band score of **6.0 or above in IELTS**; or
- a minimum score of **450 or above in College English Test Band 6 (CET-6)**, with proof of competency in spoken English; or
- an equivalent score in a recognised test; or
- an equivalent qualification to prove his/her English language proficiency, which will be considered on a case-by-case basis.
For IELTS and TOEFL qualifications for admission purposes, the University accepts only results from a single test sitting. The test must be conducted at a recognised test centre and fall within the **two-year validity period**, counted from the date of submission of the admission application for the specific intake cohort.
For CET-6 results submitted for admission purposes, the University accepts only those obtained within the **five-year validity period**, counted from the date of submission of the admission application for the specific intake cohort. Applicants must also demonstrate competency in spoken English through an oral interview conducted by the Programme and/or obtain **grade B or above in the CET-6 Speaking English Test**.
For supporting documents, applicants should submit one of the following original valid official English test reports or proof of English-medium instruction:
- TOEFL: Internet-based: **79 or above**
- IELTS (Academic): Band **6.0 or above**
- CET6: Score of **450 or above**
- Certifying letter issued and stamped with official chop by the Registry of the university confirming the medium of instruction of the applicant’s **WHOLE** degree programme was English.

Program Overview.content:
The new concentration in Human Resource Analytics and Digital Transformation is designed to prepare students for a rapidly changing business landscape, where data-driven decision-making and technological expertise are critical. This concentration ensures that graduates possess a strong understanding of HR theories and practices in both local and global contexts, enabling them to leverage advanced analytics and AI to improve organisational effectiveness.
**Aims**
- **Data-Driven Decision Making** - Equip students with the skills to make strategic decisions using HR analytics and digital transformation tools, enhancing organizational efficiency and HR management practices.
- **HR Technological Proficiency** - Develop students’ expertise in HR technologies, including AI, machine learning, and HRIS, ensuring their ability to effectively integrate these technologies across various HR functions.
- **Analytical and Strategic Application in People Management** - Empower students to apply organisational behaviour (OB) concepts to analyze HR data, predict employee behavior, and align HR strategies with broader organizational goals
- **Ethical and Innovative Practices** - Foster the ability to evaluate and implement HR strategies that are ethical, socially responsible, and innovative, particularly in the context of digital transformation and data privacy.
- **Professional Development** - Prepare students for leadership roles in HR analytics and digital transformation by providing hands-on experience, industry-relevant skills, and opportunities for internships and placements, thereby enhancing their employability.
On completing the Programme with new HRADT concentration, students will be able to explain the evolving role of digital transformation in HR management and its implications for HR policies, planning, and practices, including the integration of AI-driven innovations and data analytics; apply data-driven decision-making skills and digital tools to manage and develop people effectively in dynamic environments; demonstrate critical and innovative thinking in solving complex HR problems using AI, big data, and digital transformation strategies; utilise organisational behaviour concepts and advanced HR analytics to identify, analyse, and resolve people management issues; evaluate ethical and legal frameworks related to data privacy, diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) in HR; and develop and communicate effective HR strategies that align with organisational goals, integrate advanced technologies, and demonstrate the strategic value of HR through data-driven insights and presentations.

Curriculum.content:
This is a full-time, credit-based postgraduate programme. All courses in the Programme carry 3 credits. Students must obtain a minimum of **30 credits**, which consist of **5 required courses (15 credits)**, **4 elective courses (12 credits)** and the year course of **Action Learning Projects (3 credits)** in order to graduate. The normal duration for the Programme is **one year full-time** and the maximum period of study is **three years**. Teaching normally begins in late August and ends in May. Classes will normally be held on Lingnan's Campus.
Required courses:
1. HRM541: Human Resource Analytics (3 credits)
2. HRM542: Human Resource Information System (3 credits)
3. HRM543: New Compliance of HR Policy (3 credits)
4. HRM544: Digital Adoption and Transformation (3 credits)
5. MGT504: Contemporary Human Resource Management (3 credits)
6. MGT506: Action Learning Projects (Year-course) (3 credits)
Elective courses#:
1. MGT601 Managing Conflict in Organisations (3 credits)
2. MGT602 Leadership in Organisations (3 credits)
3. MGT604 Strategic Management (3 credits)
4. MGT605 Managing Quality for People and Organisations (3 credits)
5. MGT606 Organisational Analysis and Change (3 credits)
6. ORM515 Business Decision Making with Software (3 credits)
7. MGT501 Management of Organisations and People (3 credits)
8. MGT507: Employee Learning and Career Development (3 credits)
9. ACT615 Introduction to Python Programming (3 credits)
10. MGT502 Managing Ethically (3 credits)
11. ORM545 Cloud-based Solutions for Digital Business Transformation (3 credits)
#: The elective courses offered may vary from year to year. You are required to indicate your preference on the elective courses but the final decision rest on the Programme.

Cost of Attendance.content:
It is recommended that students prepare a budget of HK$6,200 - $7,500 to cover their first month's expenses.
The estimated monthly expenses may vary depending on individual lifestyle and spending habits. The following table is provided for general reference only:
| Item | Approx. expenses per month (HKD) |
| --- | --- |
| Meals (on campus) | HK$4,500 - $5,000 |
| Entertainment | HK$600 - $700 |
| Transportation (local) | HK$600 - $800 |
| Miscellaneous | HK$500 - $1,000 |
| **Total** | **HK$6,200 - $7,500** |

Financial Aid.content:
**Entrance Scholarship**
Entrance Scholarship will be offered to outstanding applicants and all students admitted to MScHROM will be automatically qualified for the entrance scholarship.
**Performance Scholarship**
Performance Scholarship will be awarded to the students with remarkable academic performance in every academic year.
**Professor Dean Tjosvold Scholarship**
Professor Dean Tjosvold Scholarship will be awarded to one MScHROM programme student who has outstanding academic achievements with a Grade Point Average (GPA) of 3 or above in each academic year.

Multiple Applications.content: You are required to submit separate applications if you wish to make multiple applications for different programmes of our School. Please also note that multiple application fees should be paid. Your chance of success will not be affected. However, applicants are not encouraged to switch to another programme once an admission offer has been accepted. Please be aware that the deposit fee will not be refunded if you decide to switch to another programme.

Deferral Admission Policy.content:
An applicant who has been offered admission to an approved programme of study is required to register with the Programme Office on a specified date and is considered to have been admitted to such programme on the date of his/her first registration. Registration includes payment of the fees due and enrolment and selection of courses/sections. An applicant who fails to pay the prescribed fees or register on the relevant specified dates is considered as having forgone his/her place offered by the University.
A student who for special reasons seeks permission for deferment of his/her registration may apply in writing to the Programme Director at least **one week before the specified date for registration**. A fee for late registration will be charged by the Programme Office.

Conditional Admission Policy.content:
- **Preparatory Courses Requirement for HRADT Concentration:** The preparatory course list for HRADT Concentration includes **Python**. All applicants will be required to attend a Python preparatory course unless they receive special approval from the Programme Director; such approval will be based on evidence of advanced coding experience or obtainment of relevant certifications.
- A **Human Resource Management** preparatory course will also be provided for HRADT concentration students who do not have a background in Human Resources or related fields for optional study before programme commencement.
